_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Early Peoples and Bantu Migration
910.label: Event
910.description: Hunter-gatherer Pygmy peoples (Mbuti, Twa) inhabit the Ituri rainforest; Bantu-speaking farmers migrate into the Congo Basin bringing agriculture and ironworking.

910.name: Mbuti, Twa, and Forest Peoples
910.label: Event
910.description: Indigenous hunter-gatherer communities in the equatorial forest; symbiotic relationships with later Bantu farming arrivals.

910.name: Bantu Expansion into the Congo Basin
910.label: Event
910.description: Bantu-speaking farmers spread across the Congo Basin; introduce iron smelting, pottery, and banana cultivation; population growth transforms the landscape.

920.name: Kongo Kingdom
920.label: Event
920.description: The Kongo Kingdom, centered on Mbanza-Kongo, becomes one of Africa's most powerful states; early contact with Portugal; Christianity adopted; kingdom fragmentsover time.

920.name: Foundation and Expansion of Kongo
920.label: Event
920.description: Lukeni lua Nimi founds the Kongo Kingdom; capital at Mbanza-Kongo; control of trade in copper, iron, raffia, and nzimbu shell currency.

920.name: Portuguese Contact and Afonso I
920.label: Event
920.description: Diogo Cão reaches Kongo 1482; King Afonso I converts to Christianity; diplomatic relations with Portugal and the Vatican; slave trade begins.

920.name: Luba and Lunda Empires
920.label: Event
920.description: The Luba and Lunda empires dominate the savanna of southeastern Congo; sophisticated political systems, copper/salt trade, and far-reaching influence.

920.name: Luba Empire
920.label: Event
920.description: Luba kingdom in the Upemba Depression; sacred kingship (mulopwe); elaborate political philosophy; copper-cross currency; ironworking centres.

920.name: Lunda Empire and Mwata Yamvo
920.label: Event
920.description: Lunda Empire expands under the Mwata Yamvo title; extensive tributary system; trade in slaves, ivory, and wax reaching both Atlantic and Indian Ocean coasts.

930.name: Slave Trade and European Exploration
930.label: Event
930.description: Atlantic and East African slave trades devastate the population; Arab-Swahili traders penetrate from the east; Stanley's exploration opens the Congo to European imperialism.

930.name: Atlantic Slave Trade from Congo
930.label: Event
930.description: Millions enslaved from the Congo region; Loango, Cabinda, and Kongo ports; internal wars fuelled by demand for captives; demographic catastrophe.

930.name: Arab-Swahili Slave and Ivory Trade
930.label: Event
930.description: Tippu Tip and other traders establish slaving networks from Zanzibar deep into eastern Congo; Manyema devastated; Nyangwe massacre 1871.

940.name: King Leopold's Congo Free State (1885–1908)
940.label: Event
940.description: King Leopold II's personal colony; rubber terror regime kills millions; mutilations and forced labour; international outcry leads to Belgian takeover.

940.name: Berlin Conference and Congo Free State
940.label: Event
940.description: Berlin Conference (1884–85) recognises Leopold's International Association as sovereign of the Congo; Force Publique established; rubber exploitation begins.

940.name: Rubber Terror and Atrocities
940.label: Event
940.description: Forced rubber quotas enforced by mutilation (hand-cutting), hostage-taking, and murder; population estimated to have halved; Casement Report (1904) and E.D. Morel's campaign expose horrors.

950.name: Independence, Lumumba, and Congo Crisis
950.label: Event
950.description: Rapid decolonisation; Patrice Lumumba becomes first PM; Congo Crisis erupts with Katanga secession, Lumumba assassination, and UN intervention.

950.name: Independence and the Congo Crisis
950.label: Event
950.description: Congo independent 30 June 1960; Force Publique mutiny; Katanga secession under Tshombe; Lumumba assassinated January 1961 with Belgian and CIA complicity; UN intervention.

950.name: Katanga Secession and Resolution
950.label: Event
950.description: Moïse Tshombe declares Katanga independent backed by Belgian mining interests and mercenaries; UN operations end secession by January 1963.

950.name: Mobutu and Zaïre (1965–1997)
950.label: Event
950.description: Mobutu Sese Seko seizes power; renames country Zaïre; Authenticité campaign; Cold War ally; massive corruption; economic collapse; ousted by AFDL.

950.name: Mobutu's Coup and Consolidation
950.label: Event
950.description: Lieutenant-General Mobutu seizes power November 1965; single-party MPR state; nationalises Union Minière (Gécamines); Zaïrianisation of economy.

950.name: Authenticité and Cold War Patronage
950.label: Event
950.description: Country renamed Zaïre; Authenticité campaign; Shaba invasions repelled with Western help; Mobutu as Cold War anti-communist ally; kleptocracy hollows out the state.

960.name: Congo Wars: Africa's World War
960.label: Event
960.description: Two Congo Wars (1996–97, 1998–2003) draw in nine African nations; estimated 5.4 million excess deaths; deadliest conflict since WWII.

960.name: First Congo War (1996–1997)
960.label: Event
960.description: Rwanda and Uganda back AFDL; Rwandan Hutu refugee camps dismantled; Kabila topples Mobutu; DRC declared.

960.name: Second Congo War (1998–2003)
960.label: Event
960.description: Kabila turns against Rwandan/Ugandan allies; nine African nations involved; RCD and MLC rebel groups; Lusaka Ceasefire; Laurent Kabila assassinated January 2001; Joseph Kabila succeeds.

960.name: Post-War DRC: Kabila Era and Beyond
960.label: Event
960.description: Transitional government; Joseph Kabila's presidency; delayed elections; Felix Tshisekedi elected 2019; ongoing eastern insurgency; conflict minerals.

960.name: Joseph Kabila Presidency
960.label: Event
960.description: Joseph Kabila oversees transition; elections 2006 and 2011; refuses to leave after term expires; eventually transfers power to Tshisekedi 2019.

960.name: Eastern DRC: Endless Insurgency
960.label: Event
960.description: Over 100 armed groups in Kivu; CNDP, M23, ADF-NALU, Mai-Mai; Rwanda-backed M23 captures Goma 2012 and resurges 2022–2023; MONUSCO peacekeeping.
